A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched across reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data validation, image-classification experiments, partition and regularization analyses, and training-time measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds backbone comparisons, local-training controls, and a FedFisher comparison in Section 4.5 and Supplementary F–G.

M1.justification: Both versions use pre-trained feature extraction, local least-squares learning, pairwise absolute aggregation, and regularization introduced locally and removed after aggregation. v2 expands Algorithm 1 with explicit server orchestration and returns, documenting the existing procedure. Testing additional backbones does not introduce a new AFL component.

E1.justification: Named coverage remains CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, synthetic dummy data, and ImageNet-1k pretraining. The additional backbone tests use retained datasets. However, Supplementary G does not identify the dataset used for its new FedFisher comparison, preventing a definitive judgment about whether all added evaluations remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The seven comparators in the main non-IID comparison remain unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. v2 adds FedFisher in Supplementary G and local training without aggregation as a control in Supplementary F. These additions are confined to separate comparisons.

E3.justification: The training-efficiency evaluation extends from 200 communication rounds in v1 Figure 2 to 500 in v2 Figure 3, with the 500-round budget explicitly stated in Supplementary E. New protocols include VGG11 and ViT-B-16 configurations, local-only controls, and a 50-client FedFisher comparison using a separately sourced pre-trained ResNet-18. The PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing dummy-data validation, client-count and heterogeneity analyses, and RI sensitivity tests are retained. v2 adds two focused checks: dependence on backbone choice in Section 4.5, and whether aggregation remains beneficial with pre-trained features in Supplementary F, using local maximum and average accuracy as controls.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs for the main comparison, including zero standard deviations for AFL. Dummy-data validation averages five runs in both versions. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Main-table baseline values change: at α=0.1, FedAvg changes from 53.78% to 56.62% on CIFAR-100 and from 43.54% to 46.04% on Tiny-ImageNet; AFL's corresponding results remain unchanged. These revisions accompany a longer reported training budget. v2 also adds backbone and local-control results, plus AFL 35.87% versus FedFisher 19.31% in a separate setting. Reported speedups change from 50–100× to 150–200× alongside the extended baseline budget.

T1.justification: The lemma, AA and RI-AA theorems, formal assumptions, and proof strategies are retained. However, v2 Supplementary Eq. (A.14) replaces the final X_u† factor in v1 Eq. (29) with X_u. This introduces a non-equivalent factor into the lemma's derivation, apparently through a transcription error.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's repeated claim to be the first hyperparameter-free method in FL history and explicitly scopes the title, abstract, and introduction to FL with pre-trained models. It emphasizes fast convergence and communication reduction while retaining the central one-epoch, single-round, and partition-invariance claims. The narrower claim that RI avoids tuning γ remains.

C2.justification: v2 retains the pre-trained-backbone limitation and adds substantive boundaries concerning partial participation, waiting for stragglers, and linear classifiers' suitability for nonlinear data. Section 5 discusses possible nonlinear extensions as future work. New interpretations also explain similar baseline performance through stabilization from pretraining and use local-only results to argue that collaboration remains beneficial.

D1.justification: Supplementary E supplies implementation information largely absent from v1: one local epoch, full participation, batch size 64, SGD with learning rate 0.05, RTX 4090 hardware, implementation sources, and baseline tuning grids and selected values. It also specifies reporting the best accuracy during training. Supplementary D identifies App_Dummy.ipynb, replacing v1's unresolved appendix reference; the main code URL is retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning within FL using pre-trained models, adding discussion and citations concerning parameter-efficient tuning, prototypes, prompts, and pretraining's effects. Supplementary G introduces comparison and mechanistic positioning against FedFisher. This accompanies withdrawal of the broad first-ever hyperparameter-free novelty claim; publication updates to retained works are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The title, author and affiliation block, motivation, contribution wording, and recurring terminology are edited, including replacing 'weight-invariant property' with 'invariance to data partitioning.' Dummy validation moves to Supplementary D, limitations receive a standalone section, and pseudocode becomes more explicit. Much of the retained methodological, related-work, and proof exposition closely follows v1.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, including the proofs. v2 adds an AFL overview diagram and backbone, local-control, and FedFisher tables; relocates dummy validation to the supplement; and extensively resizes and rearranges existing displays. The convergence plots also receive an extended communication-round axis.

improvement.justification: Supplementary E's implementation and tuning details improve reproducibility, while clearer pre-trained-model scope, substantive limitations, and additional controls improve interpretation. These benefits support a limited net quality gain. The new pseudoinverse omission in Eq. (A.14) weakens mathematical precision, the FedFisher dataset remains unspecified, and the larger reported speedups reflect a longer baseline budget rather than faster AFL execution.
